import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
source8 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_8.csv", index_col=0)
source9 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/training_9.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source9_34_9 and Source9_34_0 on ROW_WID
result = pd.merge(source9, source0, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Step 2: Join with Source9_34_3 on ROW_WID
result = pd.merge(result, source3, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Step 3: Join with Source9_34_4 on ROW_WID
result = pd.merge(result, source4, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Step 4: Union Source9_34_2, Source9_34_5, Source9_34_6, Source9_34_8 (all have same schema)
union_result = pd.concat([source2, source5, source6, source8], ignore_index=True)

# Step 5: Join the unioned dimension table with the current result on ROW_WID
result = pd.merge(result, union_result, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Step 6: Join with Source9_34_1 on ROW_WID
result = pd.merge(result, source1, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Step 7: Join with Source9_34_7 on ROW_WID
result = pd.merge(result, source7, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# Step 8: Group by ROW_WID and aggregate KEYWORDS_NUM by sum
# Note: KEYWORDS_NUM is from source9, after joins it remains in result
final = result.groupby("ROW_WID", as_index=False).agg({"KEYWORDS_NUM": "sum"})

# The target schema is only ['KEYWORDS_NUM'], so project only that column
final = final[["KEYWORDS_NUM"]]

# Write the final output
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_34/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
